title_original: IDA Awards Nominations: ‘Concrete Land’ Lands 6, With ‘To Hold A Mountain’ Close Behind; Elizabeth Holmes Doc In The Mix
excerpt_original: Concrete Land, which has received little attention in the U.S. so far, surprised with a leading six nominations Tuesday as the 42nd IDA Documentary Awards announced its nominees. Sundance winner To Hold a Mountain came in close behind with five. Concrete Land, directed by…

blocks.text: Concrete Land , which has received little attention in the U.S. so far, surprised with a leading six nominations Tuesday as the 42nd IDA Documentary Awards announced its nominees. Sundance winner To Hold a Mountain came in close behind with five.

Concrete Land , directed by Asmahan Bkerat, centers on the the Najar family, “one of the last Afro-Palestinian Bedouin families near Amman,” who face eviction as luxury villas encroach on their land. It won the Grierson Award at the BFI London Film Festival last month but has otherwise largely gone under the radar. Along with Best Documentary Feature, it is nominated for Best Production, Best Documentary Not in the English Language, Best Editing, Best Sound Design, and Best Writing.

blocks.text: Joining Concrete Land in the marquee Best Documentary Feature category is To Hold a Mountain , directed by Biljana Tutorov and Petar Glomazić. That film – Montenegro’s choice for the Oscar category of Best International Feature – tells the story of Gara, a remarkable woman who is determined to shield her daughter from harm while simultaneously attempting to prevent the Montenegrin government from turning beloved mountain pastures into a military training ground.

blocks.text: Also nominated for Best Documentary Feature: A Fox Under a Pink Moon , directed by Mehrdad Oskouei and Soraya Akhlaghi; Rehearsals for a Revolution , directed by Pegah Ahangarani, and You Can See Everything , directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim.

blocks.alt: Nathan Fielder in a scene from the documentary 'You Can See Everything'
blocks.caption: Nathan Fielder in ‘You Can See Everything’ A24 / Everett Collection

blocks.text: The latter film, the box office smash about imprisoned Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, earned three nominations overall, including Best Director and Best Original Music Score, recognizing composer Ari Balouzian. Rehearsals for a Revolution and A Fox Under a Pink Moon landed four nominations apiece.

blocks.caption: ‘Rehearsals for a Revolution’ Sony Pictures Classics

blocks.text: Rehearsals for a Revolution (primarily in Farsi), A Fox Under a Pink Moon (in Farsi, Dari, and Turkish) and Concrete Land (primarily in Arabic) earned nominations for Best Documentary Not in the English Language. Curiously, To Hold a Mountain , in Montenegrin, didn’t earn a nomination in that category. Had it done so, it would have tied with Concrete Land for a leading six nominations.

blocks.alt: Janay Boulous (right) and Abd Alkader Habak in 'Birds of War'
blocks.caption: Janay Boulous (right) and Abd Alkader Habak in ‘Birds of War’ Sonja Henrici Create/Habak Films

blocks.text: Birds of War , directed by Janay Boulos and Abd Alkader Habak, scored three nominations – for Best Documentary Not in the English Language, Best Writing (for Jonathan Key, Janay Boulos, and Abd Alkader Habak), and Best Original Music Score, recognizing composers Harpal Mudhar and Darren Sng.

My Undesirable Friends: Part II – Exile , Julia Loktev’s follow up to her Oscar-shortlisted My Undesirable Friends: Part I – Last Air in Moscow , earned two nominations: for Best Director and Best Editing (recognizing Loktev and Michael Taylor). Closure , directed by Michał Marczak, and Nuisance Bear , directed by Gabriela Osio Vanden and Jack Weisman, both earned two nominations each, for Best Cinematography and Best Sound Design.

Also of note are nominations for Oscar winner Laura Poitras – for her short documentary They’re Here , co-directed with Rachel Lauren Mueller; Oscar winner Ahmir “Questlove” Thompson, nominated for Best Music Documentary for Earth, Wind & Fire (To Be Celestial vs. That’s the Weight of the World) , and Oscar winner Morgan Neville, nominated for Best Music Documentary for Man on the Run . Prominent Hollywood hitmakers Baz Luhrmann and Paris Barclay earned nominations for their music documentaries – Luhrmann for EPiC: Elvis Presley in Concert , and Barclay for Billy Preston: That’s The Way God Planned It .
The 42 nd IDA Documentary Awards will take place Friday, December 4, at The Ebell of Los Angeles, hosted by Tabitha Jackson, head of Film Forum and former director of the Sundance Film Festival.

In a statement, IDA board president Ina Fichman said, “I couldn’t be more excited to celebrate these meaningful and creative documentaries. It’s a challenging time for documentary makers, but also a really inspiring moment for IDA and for the field. This year we see nominees whose deeply personal stories share narratives of resistance and exile, and we see artful, innovative filmmaking that is capturing new and robust audiences. I hope many will join us on December 4th as we honor our incredible community.”

The IDA says it received a record 650 entries in all categories from 95 countries, “an increase over last year both in the total number of entries and the countries represented. This year, 32 countries are represented among the nominees.” IDA members from around the world vote to determine the winners in the Best Feature Documentary and Best Short Documentary categories (balloting began November 17 and extends to November 29). All other category winners are selected by juries representing the international documentary community.

The 42nd Annual IDA Documentary Awards will also present the following special honors: the Career Achievement Award for the late Chilean filmmaker Patricio Guzmán ; the Truth to Power Award for Amy Goodman and Juan González of Democracy Now! ; the Emerging Filmmaker Award for Maia Lekow and Christopher King (directors of How to Build a Library ); and the Amicus Award for Cannes Docs , the documentary program of the Marché du Film led by Pierre-Alexis Chevit.
